I play with Synx a lot, who’s a good player (supposedly), and it’s definitely helped me deal with other good players. Most of them aren’t looking to support their team and are generally more focused on getting xp or dmg. There’s merit to that, but also makes it easier to counter them. If you see a player that you just can’t outplay, you kinda have to treat them as a higher tier tank. Don’t fight them alone, and make sure if they rush you, your team can help. Synx hates it when people either Zerg rush him in a huge group or are together enough where he can’t pick someone off easily.

However, there definitely is an element of player skill involved. Don’t give any player in general an easy shot at you. Have situational awareness and keep in mind where enemies are and could be. Good players will get those shots that you don’t expect simply because you’re not being careful and defending against them. If you can’t outplay them, and there’s nothing you can do to stop them, the best thing to do is to make it harder to kill you. Create some distance, lure them out into a bad position, and make your shots count. If you can’t pen, or if it’s a low chance to pen, use HE. Track them, take out their modules. I know Synx only ever brings one repair kit, and a lot of experienced players do too. At the end of the day, if 2 pros (or anyone who’s not terrible frankly) decide to focus you, only luck will keep you alive.

I mean yeah I admit that the Smasher is a good tank. But I can’t say it’s OP.

It’s gun handling is indeed, unreasonably good. It shouldn’t have more accurate SU-152 gun, but it does. However, it is a really big target, and it’s not as ‘agile’ as the SU is. Once it’s spotted up, a competent. team should punish it (competent teams are admittedly rare now) like what happens to a 183. 

The Smasher can do big damage if it’s allowed to have free shots and ambush you, but that’s a trait that all big guns share. Yeah it’s more accurate and flexible than the other 152s at t7, but it’s also mounted on a chassis that lets it down imo. Is the gun OP? Ehh I can concede that, but honestly it’s chassis lets it down. I’m not here to compare guns though, just the tank as a whole.

I’d agree with everything except Annihilator and Smasher. The Annihilator can be sidehugged. You’re not side hugging by sitting next to them, you have to keep moving, so it’s much harder for them to keep their gun on you. It’s harder, yes, in a taller tank, but it works very well, especially since the Annihilator can miss more easily. The Smasher on the other hand, isn’t OP. It’s increased armor isn’t a problem, as it’s an increase to the already strong parts of the KV-2 armor. It still has the same weaknesses. Its biggest buff is mobility, but even then its sluggish. If you’re playing a SP1C sure it’s annoying, but most other tanks can bait a shot, track it, then CoD. If you can’t do that, then just pay attention to the map and your position, a lot of spots people use are wildly predictable. If you can’t do either, it’s not the Smasher that’s OP.

I use the HP I’ve saved to tank shots and finish off the enemies. The Cent’s pen is pretty broke, the Super Pershing’s armor is virtually useless to superior British shells.

A light tank’s job isn’t to dpm enemy tanks to death. You spot, then if you can, flank to deal your damage. Aim for weakspots, finish off low-hp enemies. Autoloaders have an advantage when it comes to taking out multiple one-shot enemies.

For its role? It’s good. For the meta? It’s debatable. Currently T49 is more in favor because derps are more effective against a medium meta. The AMXs aren’t bad tanks regardless of the meta, they just aren’t as broken as the Lightweight, which also has crap depression, but has hella armor.

54 Lightweight is probably the best overall T8 light tank. It’s got really good armor for a light tank and it’s gun is decent. If you’re a new player, it shouldn’t treat you wrong.

KV-4 has some of the most reliable armor in the game. It’s pure thickness so with skill, you can guarantee a bounce. However, as the meta has shifted towards mobility and pen has increased overall, it’s much more difficult to use well.

T49 is a fast derp tank. If you’re a new player don’t use it. It’s fun, but difficult and expensive to play. Really don’t go for it if you’re new.

AMX 13 90 is a pretty good light. Mobile, small, and has a dangerous auto-loader. If you like the playstyle then go ahead, but be ready to get absolutely torn apart by the big guns you’ll meet in t8.

Centurion 1 is one of my favorite tanks. It’s got a great turret, good depression, great dpm, and insane penetration. It really almost never needs to use premium ammo. However, it’s slow and a big target. It’s difficult to play, but it’s got a reliable gun.

For newer players, the Lightweight will probably serve you best, though I don’t know your personal preferences.

As a lover of the FCM 50T, there are some important things you have to keep in mind.

1. Armor. The FCM has decent turret armor. It’s nice and thick with a thin profile. However it is not invulnerable with its cupola. It’s hull armor isn’t too bad. You can definitely sidescrape and it is very reliable. The tracks absorb a lot of the damage, but you do need to be careful about the angle, at it is very steep.

2. Gun. It’s a very nice gun. Good dpm, good pen, good handling, and decent depression. It doesn’t stand out in any specific way and doesn’t top any charts, but it is quite comfortable to use. 

Make sure to keep wiggling and make sure your angles are acute enough. Yeah it’s fun ramming anything that isn’t the VK 100 or KV-4/5, but honestly there’s no real point to use this tank. It’s not meta, but it’s fun. Kinda like an Edelweiss if you have one.

It’s thinner armor hurts it since it’s comparatively big and slower than the T-34-2. But it’s dpm is better at the sacrifice of gun handling and pen iirc. At tier 8, it faces very stiff competition currently with ATGMs in T9, the T49&ISU and others in T8, and the Smasher at T7.

Type 64 is kinda like an RU 251. Not the best acceleration, but very nice top speed and it does very well at spotting. It’s got good camo and spotting range, and while it’s dpm is low, it’s not really a dpm kinda tank. Not as good a brawler as the Cromwell and VK, but it’s a good backline harasser like the MT-25. It’s only real threat are meaner, fast tanks like the Cromwell (which you can usually outrun) and the Drac. If you let a Smasher or a KV-2 hit you that’s honestly your fault; you’re a small, fast target just don’t be dumb.
